subject: Food Science
title: Sterilization vs. Pasteurization
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Sterilization vs. Pasteurization.

hook.text: UHT milk lasts 6 months unrefrigerated. Regular pasteurized milk spoils in 2 weeks. The difference is 63 degrees.

buildup.text: Pasteurization (72°C, 15 seconds) kills pathogens. Sterilization (135°C, 2 seconds) kills virtually everything.

discovery.text: UHT milk is commercially sterile—no living microbes. Pasteurized milk still contains heat-resistant sporeformers.

twist.text: Higher heat means more nutrient loss and flavor change. UHT milk has a slight cooked taste most Europeans accept.

climax.text: In France, 95% of milk sold is UHT—no refrigeration needed. In the US, it's under 10%—consumers prefer fresh taste.

punchline.text: Kill some microbes—two week shelf life. Kill all of them—six months.

quiz.question: What is the main difference between pasteurization and UHT sterilization?
options: UHT uses higher heat to kill virtually all microbes for months of shelf life
